slides.title: AI Updates Nvidia Nemotron 3 Nano released Dec
slides.text: AI Updates Nvidia Nemotron 3 Nano released Dec 15 Super and Ultra are planned for the first half of 2026 Nvidia Nemotron-3 is a family of open-weight LLMs aimed at efficient agentic AI Three sizes: Nano (30B), Super (100B), and Ultra (500B) High throughput and strong reasoning/conversation performance Using a hybrid Mamba-Transformer Sparse MoE design ~1M-token context (Nano) Summarization, retrieval, and assistant workflows Super & Ultra adding techniques like LatentMoE, multi-token prediction, and NVFP4 training for efficiency on NVIDIA hardware Abacus AI vs Manus AI Review: Viral Hype vs Reality (2025) Abacus AI’s DeepAgent is a practical, good-value automation- coding agent today, while Manus AI is largely viral hype with major reliability, access, and pricing frustrations The video contrasts Abacus’s low-cost “all-in-one” model access with Manus’s invite/beta constraints and frequent failures Abacus DeepAgent offers access to many major models and is positioned as a straightforward subscription that became “unlimited” at a low monthly price, with users reportedly building real apps/sites quickly Manus is described as highly hyped - but then disappointing in day-to-day use (crashes, frozen tasks, empty downloadable outputs, and strict session limits https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DiWX8Pagq1k Manus released version 1.6 featuring Manus Max Improved task completion rates and 19.2% higher user satisfaction Can handle complex workflows with minimal supervision New capabilities include mobile app development and Design View offering interactive visual editing with point-and-click adjustments https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXMrezKs8Hw

slides.title: AI Updates Google Gemma 4 Run model on-device
slides.text: AI Updates Google Gemma 4 Run model on-device (phone/laptop) for near-instant responses, stronger privacy because data stays local, and predictable costs because you deploy once instead of paying usage-based inference Smaller Gemma variants can be compact (hundreds of MB at full precision, smaller when quantized), making them easier to ship inside apps and use offline The presenter describes a workflow where you can fine-tune a Gemma model, convert/quantize it (e.g., to low-bit formats), and then deploy it in lightweight experiences like a simple browser-based HTML UI, positioning this as a path to build “local copilots” for writing/coding or small business tools https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k9KLsVL4RUo OpenAI GPT Image 1.5 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U8T-Zf-xYmw Higher-quality, more reliable images and edits Better prompt instructions following Faster (up to 4x) and more cost-efficient, with reduced API costs for image generation and editing A dedicated “Images” tab in ChatGPT, offering preset filters and prompt suggestions Nano Banana Pro (Gemini Pro Image) is ahead of GPT Image 1.5 on Image Arena. It is available through Google AI Pro ($20/mo), Vertex AI, Google Workspace, and Gemini Enterprise

slides.title: AI Updates Gemini Super Gems - Free workflow
slides.text: AI Updates Gemini Super Gems - Free workflow tool https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1choivCbZDg Create automated workflows and mini apps Integrating Opal workflow builder directly into the Gemini web app The visual editor converts prompts into editable step-by-step workflows. Advanced users can access the full Opal Builder for granular control All existing Opal apps are being migrated to "My Gems from Labs" within the Gemini Gems Manager, where users can create, edit, and share custom AI assistants The feature seamlessly integrates with Google Workspace It also supports multimodal AI capabilities (images, audio, video) This feature competes with platforms like N8N Claude Chrome browser extension Claude AI appears as a side panel - for Max subscribers Powered by Claude Sonnet 4.5 and can read webpage content, click buttons, fill forms, type text, and navigate websites using natural language commands When you give Claude instructions, it can observe your screen and interact with pages through Chrome's automation APIs, simulating mouse clicks and keystrokes An orange hue appears in tab borders when Claude is actively working Claude can manage multiple browser tabs simultaneously Schedule tasks to run daily, weekly, monthly, or annual schedules Shortcuts for frequently used prompts and /slash commands Claude can handle complex multi-step tasks and continues working even when you switch tabs, with notifications when it needs permission or finishes Built-in knowledge of popular platforms like Slack, Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Docs, and GitHub You can choose between two permission modes: "Ask before acting" (Claude requests approval for each action) or "Act without asking" (autonomous operation) You can also set permissions for specific websites and change settings anytime The extension implements multiple protective measures including site-level permissions, action confirmations, and high-risk website blocking, which reduced attack success rates from 23.6% to 11.2% in testing. slides.title: Scaling Laws For Multi-agent Systems Scaling laws for
slides.text: Scaling Laws For Multi-agent Systems Scaling laws for multi-agent LLM systems https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IvJgrwp1VUk The video explains new scaling laws for multi-agent LLM systems from a Google Research, Google DeepMind, and MIT paper, “Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems.” The key claim is that “more agents” does not automatically yield better performance Performance depends on task structure, tool density, and coordination topology The authors benchmark five architectures (single, independent, centralized, decentralized, hybrid) across three model families (GPT‑5 variants, Gemini 2.x, Claude Sonnet 3.7–4.5) on four tasks: finance (parallelizable), web browsing, Minecraft-like planning, and a tool-heavy workbench. arxiv+1 ​ Findings: multi-agent systems can give up to ~80% gains on highly parallel finance-style tasks , modest gains on web navigation with decentralized debate , but cause 39–70% degradation on sequential planning tasks compared to a single agent . Tool-dense environments suffer from a “tool–coordination trade-off”: coordination chatter competes with tool specs and reasoning in the context window, increasing hallucinated tool use Independent voting ensembles amplify errors by 17.2×, centralized orchestration by 4.4×, with decentralized debate in between. arxiv+1 ​ The paper introduces a mixed-effects scaling equation showing that base model capability and task decomposability matter far more than agent count Above roughly a mid-range single-agent baseline, extra agents often hurt due to coordination overhead and error cascades, especially with many tools or strongly sequential dependencies The video’s practical advice: prefer a strong single agent for complex or tool-heavy sequential workflows, use centralized or decentralized multi-agent setups only when tasks decompose cleanly in parallel, and treat topology and context design as primary optimization levers, not agent count https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08296

slides.title: AI Updates Nous Research Nomos-1 math open-source Nous
slides.text: AI Updates Nous Research Nomos-1 math open-source Nous Research just open-sourced Nomos 1, a new 30B parameter reasoning system that scored 87 out of 120 on the 2025 Putnam Contest — crushing rivals like Qwen 3 on one of the most prestigious collegiate math competitions. https://x.com/NousResearch/status/1998536543565127968 The system uses a two-phase approach: AI ‘workers’ solve and self-critique responses, with a tournament-style bracket then selecting the best submission. Nomos’ score would have placed second among nearly 4,000 human competitors last year, with the model earning eight perfect problem scores. Nous also released and open-sourced a reasoning harness — orchestration code that manages how the model solves problems. Running Qwen3 through the same harness and setup scored just 24/120, with the result showing gains coming from model training rather than the harness.

slides.title: Get AI compliance ready for 2026 For 2026
slides.text: Get AI compliance ready for 2026 For 2026 AI compliance readiness: Create an AI system inventory (models/tools, purpose, data, vendor, jurisdictions) and run a risk program aligned to the NIST AI RMF lifecycle (govern/map/measure/manage) Prioritize high-impact uses ( hiring, housing, credit, health ) because US state rules like Colorado’s 2026 AI Act focus there, even as federal policy may move toward more unified oversight If you operate in the EU, plan for phased EU AI Act duties and keep documentation active, not just drafted. Implement: approval/change control, data governance, testing (accuracy/bias/security), human oversight, user notices, logging/monitoring, and an incident/complaints process Start a 90-day sprint: inventory + classify, stand up governance + baseline evals, then productionize controls and do a mock audit https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/12/eliminating-state-law-obstruction-of-national-artificial-intelligence-policy/

slides.title: Web Research Multi-Agent Architectures Modern LLM platforms like
slides.text: Web Research Multi-Agent Architectures Modern LLM platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude use multi-agent architectures for deep research. An orchestrator agent receives the user query, creates a research plan, and delegates tasks to specialized sub-agents that run in parallel. Web search agents explore different aspects of the topic, retrieving content and citations. Once sub-agents return findings, a synthesizer agent consolidates the information into a coherent narrative, while a citations agent ensures each claim is properly sourced. OpenAI uses reinforcement learning-trained reasoning models with interactive clarification. Gemini leverages its multimodal capabilities and proposes research plans for user approval. Claude employs clearly defined multi-agent orchestration with parallel sub-agents. Perplexity uses iterative retrieval loops with hybrid model selection. Grok processes content in segments with credibility assessment. These systems typically run fifteen to thirty minutes , performing dozens of searches and synthesizing hundreds of sources before delivering fully-cited reports. The architecture transforms vague queries into precise, machine-executable plans through planning, parallel execution with tool use, information retrieval with contextual awareness, and final synthesis into polished documents.

slides.title: AI advantage is compounding Organizations that deeply integrate
slides.text: AI advantage is compounding Organizations that deeply integrate GenAI are pulling away from laggards Higher-intensity use of AI creates non-linear gains that get reinvested into even more capability https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QONt74CTUyE Recent enterprise research (OpenAI, Menlo, an AI ROI benchmarking survey, and a new EY AI Pulse Survey) showing that AI benefits are now broadly visible, but unevenly captured A key driver is a widening “usage gap” : OpenAI’s “frontier” workers (95th percentile) use AI far more than median employees, especially on complex tasks like analysis and coding, and leading organizations shift work into reusable custom GPTs/projects that store context More breadth and depth of use correlates with higher ROI: time savings are a common entry point, but the biggest ROI comes from moving up the value chain into better decisions, new capabilities, and revenue impact Finally, winners reinvest: big AI spenders report larger productivity gains and then plow benefits back into expanding and building new AI capabilities and R&D, rather than layoffs , accelerating a flywheel toward agentic systems that require real data/tooling infrastructure

slides.title: AI Updates Prompting Claude Code / Claude Opus
slides.text: AI Updates Prompting Claude Code / Claude Opus 4.5 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xob-2a1OnvA 10 rules drawn from Anthropic guidance, replacing vague asks with structured briefs that produce consistently better work Adopt a collaborative tone, being explicit about the task (strong action verbs, desired quantity, and target audience) Set firm constraints (length, style, “do/don’t” rules) to reduce generic output Use workflow of draft/plan/act Have Claude outline first, refine the outline, and only then generate the final deliverable A major theme is forcing structure - request tables, schemas, checklists, or specific formats - so results are easier to verify and reuse Explain the “why” behind the request, and control verbosity by telling Claude which role to adopt (expert, brief, simplifier) and how detailed to be Finally, provide scaffolds/templates, use “power phrases” and personas to raise output quality, and break complex work into smaller subtasks (“divide and conquer”) Prompting Claude Code

slides.title: Apple CLaRa Framework Apple’s CLaRa AI framework CLaRa
slides.text: Apple CLaRa Framework Apple’s CLaRa AI framework CLaRa = "Continuous Latent Reasoning" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-obd_O-NCOI Goal to improve RAG. CLaRa compresses documents into dense latent memory tokens and operates retrieval and generation in a "shared continuous space", allowing the model to reason over compressed representations rather than raw text This unified approach solves the "broken gradient" problem in classic RAG by letting the generator effectively teach the retriever what information matters, improving overall relevance and performance while reducing context costs and latency The instruction-tuned "CLaRa-7B-Instruct" model supports question-answering directly from compressed representations, offering strong performance with significant compression factors Because it combines retrieval and generation in one 7-billion-parameter model, it can run on smaller hardware and handle larger document sets more efficiently CLaRa architecture could shift how RAG models are built and used, especially where combining memory, retrieval accuracy, and cost matters Apple CLaRa "Continuous Latent Reasoning" Claude Code can now directly control the browser through the /chrome command This allows Claude Code to test and validate code directly in Chrome Claude Code can open Chrome, navigate to applications, click buttons, fill forms, monitor network requests in real-time, capture console errors as they happen, and take screenshots at any viewport size The system uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol - the same API that Chrome DevTools itself uses internally - to gain direct access to the browser

slides.title: Get Rich with AI in 2026 Use AI
slides.text: Get Rich with AI in 2026 Use AI to get rich in 2026 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nqx0QjHQ9ww Getting rich with AI isn’t about linear plans or being a top coder; it’s about building fast feedback loops that compound learning and execution The video frames a coming economic shift toward exponential growth and self-improving systems, citing how quickly AI products and AI startups can scale It then teaches four loops: (1) The “balance loop”: stay on a tightrope between your asymmetric advantage (unique experience, domain knowledge, network, etc.) and a customer’s acute, frequent pain; constantly surface assumptions and validate them quickly with AI (2) The “speed-to-revenue loop”: ship, learn, and iterate daily; Cursor is used as an example of extreme shipping speed and “dogfooding” (using its own product to build itself) (3) The “signal-to-innovation loop”: treat user behavior data as the core R&D engine; YouTube’s continual experiments are contrasted with Quibi’s rigid, assumption-driven approach (4) The “sweat equity loop”: early-stage founders must stay deeply involved, sweating details as the product and market keep moving, turning persistence into long-term value

slides.title: AI Updates Integral AI = True AGI ?
slides.text: AI Updates Integral AI = True AGI ? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RVqNUUYd9UA The video covers e x-Google researcher Jad Tafari and his startup Integral AI , which claim to have built the “world’s first AGI-capable model.” Integral defines AGI with three criteria: autonomous skill learning in novel domains without human-provided datasets, safe and reliable mastery without catastrophic failures, and human-comparable energy efficiency for learning new skills. Their criticism of current LLMs is that they are black-box predictors reliant on brute-force optimization, lacking explicit world models and interpretable abstractions.[1] Integral proposes “universal simulators” that build hierarchical, multimodal world models and grow via lifelong learning without catastrophic forgetting. Demo clips show an embodied agent exploring 3D rooms to answer questions, a vision system that selectively reveals image patches like eye saccades, and a puzzle-solving “Shooan” experiment where the agent plans by estimating remaining steps to a goal. The creator notes that DeepMind published somewhat analogous imagination-augmented agents work in 2017 with peer-reviewed methods and open code, while Integral has released no benchmarks, code, or independent evaluations. He concludes the architecture ideas sound plausible, but the AGI-capable claim is unsubstantiated until rigorous external validation appears.[1] Tokyo-based Integral AI Founded by ex-Google engineer Jad Tarifi Claim - first true AGI system embodied in physical robots Their system allegedly learns new tasks autonomously without curated datasets or human labeling, using an architecture inspired by the human neocortex, and has already demonstrated successful robotic trials https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zrr3KQrQ-WA

slides.text: AI Updates Google DeepMind Interactions API (/interactions). (Similar to OpenAI Responses API) Interactions API is a unified interface for interacting with Gemini models and agents that fundamentally shifts AI development from stateless request-response patterns to stateful, multi-turn workflows https://venturebeat.com/infrastructure/why-googles-new-interactions-api-is-such-a-big-deal-for-ai-developers Lovable raises $330M at $6.6B valuation ChatGPT x Replit Launch https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Szmlj6_gbt8 Quint Code - https://github.com/m0n0x41d/quint-code Quint Code is a set of commands for AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, and Codex that implements hypothesis-driven decision making with auditable evidence trails Rather than relying on "vibe coding" where AI generates code without rigorous validation, Quint provides a framework that forces both engineers and AI to pause, validate assumptions, and document decisions systematically.​ The toolkit is based on approximately 10% of the First Principles Framework (FPF), a formal "thinking OS" specification created by Anatoly Levenchuk Quint guides users through an ADI cycle—Abduction, Deduction, and Induction generating competing hypotheses, verifying them logically, testing empirically, and producing Decision Rationale Records that document what was chosen, why, supporting evidence, rejected alternatives, and when to revisit the decision.​ Currently, Quint is a command-based toolkit with no UI or dependencies, adding minimal overhead to existing AI coding workflows. It consists of slash commands that act as structured prompts, making it harder to skip critical validation steps before code generation. The tool has been tested in complex engineering and strategy tasks with notably improved quality compared to unstructured AI interactions.​ Future version 4.0 will introduce a compact MCP server that manages the FPF kernel and invariants using local SQLite databases alongside markdown files, allowing persistent context about project constraints and past decisions to be automatically fed to AI assistants
